title: Eviction Horizon: graceful dequeue & soft-trim admission pipeline
creator: Priya Singh
description:
Problem: Regional overload spikes and cold‑start cascades are producing tail violations against our 99th percentile latency SLOs. Current token‑budget admission and coarse priority lanes are effective but too binary — they cause abrupt client visible truncation or wholesale rejects during cross‑region failover.

Goal: Implement an "eviction horizon" mechanism combined with a graceful dequeue (soft‑trim) admission pipeline that: (1) enables chronological aging and burst smoothing of queued requests, (2) performs tenant‑aware soft trimming instead of hard rejects when capacity is constrained, and (3) cooperates with circuit breaker heuristics to progressively degrade fidelity while preserving SLOs for high‑priority interactive flows.

Design summary:
- Eviction horizon: requests carry a small monotonic timestamp and an "elasticity" score derived from tenant tier, route SLO class, and request cost estimate. The horizon is a sliding window computed per-shard that favors newer interactive requests but allows long‑running queued background work to age out gracefully.
- Graceful dequeue (soft‑trim): when admission would exceed the latency headroom, we try a sequence: (a) prefix KV cache reuse and request rewrite (drop non-essential callbacks), (b) token budget trimming (truncate generation target length by %), (c) fall back to a lower‑cost model variant, (d) reject only when all soft options exhausted. Every step emits a policy tag for billing/observability.
- Chronological aging + burst smoothing: maintain two counters — instantaneous occupancy and decayed occupancy — to absorb short spikes without triggering hard shedding. Decay window tuned from production p95->p99 latency spread.
- Circuit breaker interaction: breakers transition to a 'soft' state that allows reduced‑quality responses instead of immediate open/close; integrates with rollout policies for model variant fallback.

Telemetry & metrics: new metrics needed: evicted_count, soft_trim_rate (by trim type), horizon_age_distribution, per-tenant trimming_latency_impact, policy_tag histogram. Alert rules tie to SLO burn rate and per‑region spike correlation.

Rollout plan: prototype in a single non‑critical region behind a canary gateway, run traffic replay for burst scenarios, compare p50/p95/p99 vs baseline, then staggered multi‑region rollout with circuit breaker thresholds relaxed during warmup.

Docs & links: Confluence design doc, performance microbenchmark, and a draft operator runbook are linked in attachments.

Tradeoffs considered:
- Complexity vs observability: extra policy tags and counters increase cardinality — mitigated by aggregated rollups and sample rates.
- Fairness vs latency: chronological aging slightly favors new interactive flows; mitigated via per‑tenant decay factors.
- Billing semantics for soft‑trimmed responses need PM decision (credit, partial bill, or full bill) — action item assigned below.
acceptance_criteria: API-level telemetry: horizon_age_distribution and soft_trim_rate surfaced in Console and dashboard
Prototype serving integration in canary region with automated test harness for spike scenarios
Integration tests for circuit breaker soft-state and fallback to model variants
Runbook updated with operator steps for toggling horizon aggressiveness and emergency rollback
Performance: p99 latency under target for tier-1 interactive routes during 2x synthetic burst compared to baseline
